Intrinsic (dose-dependent) hepatotoxicity occurs when a drug or its metabolite is directly cytotoxic to hepatocytes — acetaminophen (via NAPQI, its reactive quinone imine metabolite formed by CYP2E1) is the classic example. Bile salt export pump (BSEP/ABCB11) inhibition causes cholestatic liver injury by preventing bile acid secretion.

The reaction mechanism determines the sensitization potency — strong electrophiles that react with both cysteine and lysine (e.g., acid anhydrides, isocyanates) tend to be stronger sensitizers than those reacting with only one nucleophile.
